business_scope.primary_industry_name: Double-Shot PBT Plastic Injection of Novelty Keyboard Keycaps

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid bi-jural system: Civil Law for private matters in Quebec (Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c. CCQ-1991) and Common Law for public law and for private law in the other provinces; federal parliamentary democracy with provincial legislative competence over incorporation, securities and consumer protection.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention Between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (1980), as amended by Protocols of 1997 and 2007
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), Canada-EU, provisionally applied since 2017-09-21 (Investment Chapter)
Hague Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Apostille Convention, 1961), in force for Canada since 2024-01-11
Canada-UK Agreement on Trade Continuity (2021), applicable to United Kingdom-origin investment

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended (PCMLTFA); Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part II.1 (terrorist financing); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17 (SEMA); Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 10; United Nations Act, S.C. 1991, c. 45. Provincial (Quebec): Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, including the duty to declare each individual with significant control (statutory 25% ownership or control threshold) in the file of the enterprise at the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ); Regulation respecting the information obligations of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 2; Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236-2245 (societe en commandite / limited partnership). The limited partnership is transparent for income tax and is not itself an entity subject to Part XIX of the PCMLTFA, but its general partner and the payment service providers (Shopify Payments, Stripe) are reporting entities for FINTRAC purposes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the partnership agreement (contrat de societe en commandite) or, where the general partner is a foreign entity, certified copy of that entity's formation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent business registry or civil-law notary of the jurisdiction in which the document was executed or issued
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; Consular Legalization only where the country of origin is not a party to the 1961 Apostille Convention (not applicable to Canada, United States or EU member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence of the foreign general partner, dated within 30 days of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry of the general partner (e.g., Secretary of State, Companies House, or equivalent)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copies of passports of all individuals with significant control (UBOs) and of the authorized signatories of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence of each individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of each country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) designating the Quebec registered agent and the signatories empowered to file the declaration of registration with the REQ and to bind the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign notary or attorney-at-law executing the power of attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Consular Legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of Canada where the executing jurisdiction is not party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (bank statement or utility bill dated within 90 days), certified as a true copy by the issuing institution or a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution or municipal utility, certified by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing state; Consular Legalization for non-Apostille states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the general partner, all limited partners holding at least 10% economic interest, and every individual with significant control against: (1) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List administered under SEMA and the Special Economic Measures Regulations; (2) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List as implemented by regulations under the United Nations Act; (3) the Criminal Code list of terrorist entities; (4) the Global Affairs Canada listing of listed persons and entities. Because payment rails are North-American USD rails (Shopify Payments and Stripe), mandatory screening also applies against the OFAC SDN List, OFAC Sectoral Sanctions Identifications List and the U.S. Section 311 List. PEP protocol follows PCMLTFA guidance: enhanced due diligence for domestic and foreign PEPs, heads of international organizations, their family members and close associates; no automatic refusal on list hits without enhanced analysis; suspicious transaction reports to FINTRAC are triggered on any reasonable grounds; a written risk memo and source-of-funds narrative must be completed for each UBO before any capital contribution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - official online business register and filing portal, accessible at https://www.registrairedesentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; name search and reservation module: Centre d'affaires / Services en ligne - Recherche et reservation de nom
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11 (ss. 31-36), the name of an enterprise registered in Quebec must be in French in its distinctive element; the legal element must read 'societe en commandite', 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.'. A non-French distinctive element (e.g., a keyboard-cap brand) may be accepted only if it is a registered trademark within the meaning of the Trademarks Act or if it constitutes a permissible personal name; otherwise the applicant must supply a French transliteration or a French generic descriptor. Latin script is required; names may incorporate standard French diacritics; non-Latin scripts are not accepted.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: chambre de commerce, chamber of commerce
Canada, Quebec, Montreal (unless prior authorization is obtained from the competent public authority)
Red Cross, Croix-Rouge, United Nations, UNESCO
Inc., Ltd., Corp., LLC, LLP (improper legal suffixes for a Quebec limited partnership)
terms that are scandalous, obscene, contrary to public order or that imply a state monopoly or public authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A REQ name reservation is valid for 90 days and may be renewed once for an additional 90 days by filing a renewal request and paying the applicable tariff before expiry; if the limited partnership is not registered within the extended window, a fresh name search is required. Upon refusal, the applicant should first file a written request for administrative review with the REQ, supplying a revised distinctive element and legal arguments, response typically within 15 business days. If the refusal is maintained, an appeal may be brought by motion before a judge of the Court of Quebec, contestation under section 32 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, within 30 days of notification; in practice, refiling a new name with a materially different distinctive element is the fastest and most cost-effective route.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for the registered office and for service of process, provided the address is a physical street address in Quebec at which a human agent receives and signs for documents; a post-office box is not permitted. The target enterprise is an online retailer of custom mechanical keyboard keycaps using double-shot PBT plastic injection; because manufacturing is insourced or contract-manufactured at a separate plant, a virtual office satisfies the commercial-substance requirements of the REQ and of payment providers, subject to maintained books and records in Quebec.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: unannounced physical inspection probability estimated at less than 5% per annum for the registered office; Revenu Quebec and Canada Revenue Agency audits are documentary in nature and target GST/QST and payroll filings rather than premises; no storefront or local manufacturing floor is required for an e-commerce model.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed tariff: Regulation respecting the fees exigible for services rendered by the registraire des entreprises (CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 4), online name reservation fee of CAD 29.50

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed tariff: electronic certified extract fee of CAD 16.37

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary en exercice, Chambre des notaires du Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: fixed-scope notarial minute, approximately CAD 675

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille issuance for the five foreign-origin documents in the due-diligence bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec registered agent and service-of-process office (virtual office with physical street address and mail handling), year one
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate services agent in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for a Quebec registered office address for an online-only manufacturing enterprise, approximately CAD 340

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2186-2266 (governing limited partnerships); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 2, 12-18, 24-27; Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c. S-31.1 (applicable mutatis mutandis to the general partner if it is a company)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) of the limited partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for limited partnerships under the Civil Code of Québec. The capital contributions are fixed in the limited partnership agreement; limited partners must contribute the agreed amount or property in exchange for partnership interests. No provincial escrow account is mandatory, but certain aerodrome, trust company, or non-resident ownership rules may require escrow or account holds if a general partner is a corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the General Partner, acting as manager of the limited partnership (the 'Partnership'), hereby accepts the subscription for partnership participation units (intérêts) as set forth in the partnership agreement, including the agreed capital contributions of each limited partner. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Partnership be established at [street address], Montréal, Québec, in accordance with the Civil Code of Québec and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. RESOLVED FURTHER that [name] be appointed as the authorized representative (mandatary) of the Partnership, with authority to file the Declaration of Registration, receive legal notices, and open bank accounts. RESOLVED FURTHER that the General Partner and officers are authorized to execute all documents and pay all fees incidental to formation and registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Conducting name availability search and obtaining name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar) - online 'Recherche dans le registre' and 'Avis de disponibilité du nom' services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the registrar's online application, submit a name analysis request for the proposed limited partnership name containing the phrase 'Limited Partnership' or 'S.E.C.' (société en commandite), and obtain a formal name availability notice. If the name is distinctive and acceptable, request a reservation. Provide the required dossiers and pay the applicable fee.
required_dossiers: Name analysis and reservation application
Draft limited partnership agreement (if required)
Identification of the general partner (business or personal ID)
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
Proof of current Quebec address for the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to confusion with a protected name, file a written justification with supporting trademark or prior-use evidence, or submit a revised name for re-analysis. There is no additional fee for amendment if lodged promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, reviewing and executing the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or legal counsel admitted to the Barreau du Québec, in the judicial district where the registered office of the partnership will be located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the written limited partnership agreement under Civil Code of Québec arts. 2186-2229, specifying the name, head office, objects, general partner's powers, limited partners' capital subscriptions, profit/loss sharing, transfer restrictions, admission of additional partners, and dissolution provisions. Execute the agreement before a notary, or as a private writing, in as many originals as there are partners with adverse interests.
required_dossiers: Draft limited partnership agreement
Identity and address of each general and limited partner
Declaration of contributions (cash, property, or services served)
Resolution of the general partner's corporate board if the general partner is a corporate entity
Consent of each partner to the terms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agreement is found to violate mandatory provisions of the Civil Code of Québec or is incomplete, legal counsel may prepare an amending deed, and all partners execute a rectification agreement before the same authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishing registered office and appointing a representative in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (for address registration) and municipal office (for occupancy/IDM permit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a physical address in Quebec to serve as the partnership's registered office. If the general partner is not domiciled in Quebec, appoint a natural person residing in Quebec as the partnership's representative for the service of documents. Submit the office address and representative's consent to the registry as part of the registration declaration.
required_dossiers: Lease or proof of ownership of the registered office
Consent to act of the proposed representative (permanent resident in Quebec)
Identification and address of the representative
General partner's formal decision designating the office and representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal zoning officer or the registrar finds the address inadequate for a manufacturing operation, relocate the registered office or obtain a municipal zoning compliance certificate (certificat de conformité) before re-submitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (online filing portal 'Idéclare')
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the statutory Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) in French or English, entering the partnership name, registered office, general partner's full name and address, representatives (if any), and the date of formation. Attach the required dossiers, pay the registration fee by credit card or electronic funds transfer, and obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). The declaration must be filed within 60 days of the formation of the partnership.
required_dossiers: Completed registration declaration form
Copy of the limited partnership agreement (if requested)
Proof of appointment of the general partner
Name reservation notice and approved name
Identity documentation for the general partner and representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a refusal or a query, provide the requested clarifications or amendments within 15 days. If the query concerns a minor drafting error, submit a correction declaration; if a substantive omission exists, refile a sworn declaration with additional supporting documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration statutory filings (tax, municipal, and license post-registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec; Agence du revenu du Canada; Municipal licensing authority (e.g., Service des permis et inspections de Montréal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued NEQ, register for Quebec sales tax (QST), GST/HST, and payroll source deductions with Revenu Québec and the CRA as applicable. Obtain a municipal business permit for light manufacturing (if the municipal zoning regime requires), and open a business bank account under the partnership's name. Confirm eligibility for the fixed tax rate filing if the partnership has no permanent establishment in Quebec.
required_dossiers: Partnership registration confirmation (attestation d'immatriculation)
NEQ number
General partner's identification
Proof of registered office address
Municipal zoning compliance letter
Bank reference letter (if opening an account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec imposes late-filing penalties, request a penalty cancellation under the Tax Administration Act based on reasonable cause. If the municipal permit is refused, obtain a temporary municipal authorization or apply for a variance after remedying the specified deficiencies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), municipal industrial hygiene and safety inspectorate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation environnementale pour exploitation industrielle (industrial operation environmental authorization) under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Direction générale de l'évaluation environnementale et de la conformité environnementale
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Registration (Déclaration de conformité) for a small plastic injection molding establishment; a full EIA (Étude d'impact) is not required unless daily wastewater effluent or VOC emissions exceed the thresholds prescribed in the Règlement sur l'assainissement de l'atmosphère (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 4.1). For facilities emitting less than 4 tonnes of VOCs per year, an exemption applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with municipal sewer bylaws (COD ≤ 950 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 500 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.5, and no non-biodegradable solvents exceeding 5 mg/L); VOC emissions capped at 10 tonne/year per the applicable stream; plastic waste must be sorted and recycled under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products; residual materials must be managed in accordance with the Regulation respecting hazardous waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire service (e.g., Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal) under the Québec Building Code and the Fire Safety Act, confirming that the injection molding equipment and plastic resin storage areas are compliant with fire separations, sprinklers, and emergency routes. A structural load inspection by a licensed engineer must certify that the floor will support mold presses and hoppers. Occupational workplace clearance, including a CNESST risk assessment and a health and safety program, is required under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c. S-2.1).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal registration portal (Business Registration Online via https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); Revenu Québec — provincial registration portal for QST and NEQ (IN-1082 via https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The non-resident limited partnership, having a permanent establishment in Quebec, must first register through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) to obtain a federal Business Number (BN). Concurrently, the partnership appoints a Canadian-resident representative and files the Revenu Québec 'Registration Form for a Business' to obtain the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and QST registration number. Required supporting documentation includes the certified declaration of constitution, the partnership agreement identifying the general partner, details of the place of business in Quebec, and proof of authority for the agent (GST/HST Form RC59 for non-resident registrants). Registration must be completed before issuing taxable invoices; the GST/HST and QST accounts become active as of the required registration date or the voluntary election date.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — The Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the Taxation Act (Quebec); the partnership files an information return (T5013) but is not liable for income tax on its revenues. Each partner (including non-resident partners in respect of Canadian-source income) is taxable on their pro-rata share of income. However, for GST/HST/QST purposes, the partnership is treated as a separate 'person' and registrant, as provided for under the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Sales Tax Act (implied partial-taxation hybrid).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada and Quebec do not have 'check-the-box' entity classification elections; classification follows statutory rules. Available elections include: (i) partnership fiscal period election under ITA subsection 249.1(4) to adopt an off-calendar year-end and align with non-resident partners' fiscal years; (ii) election under ETA subsection 273(1) to treat a non-resident partner's supplies through the partnership as being made by the partnership (avoiding bifurcated registration); (iii) election to claim the rebate of tax paid on partnership inputs by the general partner, with the partnership receiving the rebate; (iv) hybrid mismatch remedial elections under ITA sections 18.6-18.7 and the OECD BEPS Action 2 domestic rules, which adjust deductions by reference to dual-status foreign check-the-box entities; and (v) QST input tax refund elections allowing the partnership to compute ITRs on a GST-inclusive or streamlined formula.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) — direct percentage value-added consumption taxes
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the small-supplier exemption applies where worldwide taxable supplies (excluding financial services and certain capital property sales) are less than CAD 30,000 in the current calendar quarter and the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; once exceeded, GST/HST registration becomes mandatory under ETA subsection 240(1), and the identical CAD 30,000 threshold triggers compulsory QST registration under the Quebec Sales Tax Act (CO 322 r. 2). No sector-specific threshold applies to NAICS 334118; voluntary registration is available to recover input tax credits on start-up costs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not operate mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, digital stamping, or API-based pre-clearance for e-invoices. Mandated standards include: (i) mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST returns via CRA My Business Account and QST returns via Revenu Québec CLIC; (ii) issuance of invoices in both English and French where the invoice is used in Quebec (Quebec Charter of the French Language requirements) with equivalent data on each linguistic version; (iii) record retention in XML or machine-readable formats for at least 6 years; and (iv) phased adoption of the Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework (Peppol-compatible standards, 2024-2026). No digital stamping or mandatory third-party clearance of individual invoices is required; however, the partnership must ensure its Shopify Payments/Stripe billing outputs satisfy CRA and Revenu Québec informational content requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the sale of custom mechanical keyboard caps under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 20 of the Excise Tax Act where the goods are physically exported by the supplier or caused to be exported by the non-resident purchaser, and are exported as soon as is reasonably possible after the delivery/sale. Comparable QST zero-rating applies under the Taxation Act and its regulations for goods exported to a destination outside Canada. The partnership must be a registrant, hold evidence of export within the statutory period, and the buyer must be a non-resident for GST/HST purposes. Offshore services (such as design or digital renderings supplied to non-resident clients) may also be zero-rated under Schedule VII, s. 7 of the ETA. Incoming payments through Shopify Payments or Stripe may be received in CAD or foreign currency; Canada imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for zero-rating, so the 180-day window is adopted as the internal documentary-control benchmark and general banking/customs compliance convention.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A submitted through CARM/Canadian export reporting system), including destination, value, and HS Chapter 3926/8473 classification
Commercial invoice containing the date, seller, buyer, description, unit value, export terms, and statement of origin
Bill of Lading (ocean B/L or airway bill) evidencing physical movement of the goods from Canada to the foreign destination
Packing list matching shipped SKUs (double-shot PBT novelty keycap sets) with counts synchronized to the invoice
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank wire or SWIFT MT103 record proving receipt of payment from the non-resident buyer, referencing the relevant invoice number
Sales or export contract with the foreign buyer, including Incoterms (e.g., CIP, DAP, FOB Montreal), governing law clause, and evidence of the non-resident status of the buyer
Foreign currency conversion confirmation where invoice settlement occurs in USD or EUR
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec exporter verification programs scrutinize zero-rated export claims for documentation sufficiency and diversion risk. If goods are diverted to the domestic Canadian market within two years, or documentation is incomplete, the comprehensive audits may re-assess the supply at 5% GST plus 9.975% QST, disallow related input tax credits, and assess interest from the original due date. Penalties include the ETA s. 280 false-statement penalty of 25% of the net tax amount involved, an additional gross-negligence penalty of 25%, and penalties of up to 50% for misrepresentation under Quebec civil rules. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion or fraudulently claiming zero-rating can result in fines of up to 200% of tax evaded and up to 5 years imprisonment under the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Tax Administration Act; the limitation period retroactively extends from 4 years to 7 years where misrepresentation is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration imposing currency controls, mandatory conversion, capital controls, or routine approval requirements for cross-border payments. Anti-money-laundering supervision is principally administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada, and prudential supervision of federally regulated banks is administered by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for ordinary commercial and investment transactions. Current-account payments, including imports, exports, service fees, royalties, interest, dividends, and ordinary profit distributions, generally do not require central-bank approval or conversion into Canadian dollars. Capital-account flows, including partner contributions, partnership interests, intercompany loans, acquisitions, and repatriations, are generally permitted without exchange-control approval, subject to contractual restrictions, bank compliance review, Canadian tax rules, withholding-tax obligations, sanctions, anti-money-laundering requirements, beneficial-ownership verification, and applicable reporting. A Quebec limited partnership should maintain executed partnership agreements, partner registers, contribution records, loan agreements, tax forms, invoices, and board or partner resolutions supporting the legal and commercial purpose of each transfer. Non-resident partners may generally receive distributions, but the partnership must evaluate Canadian withholding, information-return, permanent-establishment, transfer-pricing, and treaty implications before payment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general statutory deadline requiring exporters to repatriate or convert export receipts. Export proceeds may normally remain in Canadian-dollar or foreign-currency accounts, subject to the account agreement and bank controls. Large cash transactions, international electronic funds transfers, suspicious transactions, and certain cross-border transfers may trigger reporting by financial institutions or other reporting entities under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and related regulations. Customs, tax, sales-tax, sanctions, and export-control records must nevertheless be retained and reconciled with accounting records.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; separate escrow or trust account only where contractually required
Operational Account; foreign-currency account and merchant-services account available subject to underwriting
Operational Account; optional Canadian-dollar and foreign-currency settlement accounts
Operational Account; trade-finance and foreign-exchange services subject to credit and compliance approval
Operational Account; optional foreign-currency and merchant settlement facilities
Operational Account; treasury, foreign-exchange, and payment services subject to onboarding approval

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to high for payment acceptance and settlement, but not a substitute for a Canadian bank account in all use cases. Canada does not operate a single European-style electronic-money-institution licensing regime. An offshore digital EMI or payment institution may provide collection, foreign-exchange, card, or payout services only within the scope of its home-country authorization and the Canadian activities permitted by applicable law. Canadian payment-service-provider obligations under the Retail Payment Activities Act may apply to prescribed payment functions performed in Canada. Shopify Payments and Stripe availability, settlement currencies, reserve requirements, chargeback exposure, prohibited-business rules, identity verification, and Canadian tax information must be confirmed directly with each provider. Offshore wallets may be rejected for partner capital, payroll, tax remittances, regulated trust funds, or high-volume commercial flows. Maintain a Canadian operating account for tax, payroll, refunds, supplier payments, and liquidity back-up.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors or partners are not generally required by Canadian law to appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be available for Canadian or non-resident owners, but the bank may require notarized or certified identity documents, video verification, Canadian address evidence, a live compliance interview, wet signatures, or branch attendance based on risk, ownership complexity, foreign control, document jurisdiction, or inability to verify identity electronically. For a Quebec limited partnership, expect review of the limited-partnership declaration or registration evidence, partnership agreement, general-partner authority, beneficial-ownership information, business address, tax registrations, expected transaction profile, source of funds, and names of all controlling persons and authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear legal existence or mismatch between the Quebec limited partnership, its general partner, trade name, registration records, and bank application
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Quebec enterprise registration evidence, executed limited-partnership agreement, general-partner authorization, partner and beneficial-owner schedule, business-number confirmation where available, registered-office evidence, organization chart, and certified translations for non-English or non-French documents

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owners, controlling partners, or persons exercising effective control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ownership and control chart, partner register, identification documents, residential-address evidence, control-person declarations, corporate certificates for entity partners, director and officer registers, and signed beneficial-ownership certification

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership, foreign source of funds, or capital transfers from jurisdictions receiving enhanced bank scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital-contribution agreement, source-of-wealth narrative, bank statements, audited or management financial statements, tax returns where appropriate, sale or investment documents, payment-chain evidence, sanctions screening results, and a written explanation of the commercial purpose and expected counterparties

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume online sales, marketplace settlements, chargebacks, refunds, or payment flows inconsistent with the stated custom keyboard-keycap manufacturing profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Website and product catalogue, Shopify or Stripe agreements, supplier invoices, purchase orders, fulfilment records, shipping contracts, customer geographies, refund and chargeback policy, sales forecasts, expected monthly transaction volumes, and reconciliation methodology

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, unrelated third-party payment processors, nominee arrangements, cash-intensive activity, or pass-through transfers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy, account segregation plan, related-party register, payment-processor contracts, invoice-to-payment reconciliations, prohibition of personal-account use, documented approval matrix, and explanations for any historical third-party receipts

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-control, restricted-party, or politically exposed-person screening concerns involving partners, suppliers, customers, logistics providers, or payment intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty master file, screening reports, end-use and end-user statements where relevant, product classification records, shipping documentation, sanctions-policy certification, escalation records, and evidence of ongoing screening

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency uncertainty, missing Canadian tax information, or unexplained distributions to non-resident partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Partnership tax classification memorandum, CRA business-number and program-account evidence where applicable, partner tax-residency forms, treaty documentation, distribution resolutions, withholding calculations, information-return filing plan, and accountant confirmation

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent expected activity, rapid movement of inbound capital, or transfers lacking a clear payment purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling cash-flow forecast, opening balance sheet, capitalization table, funding schedule, transaction-purpose matrix, sample invoices, supplier and customer contracts, bank statements, and documented dual-approval payment controls

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route partner contributions through a Canadian bank account held in the legal name of the Quebec limited partnership or its properly authorized general partner. Use a bank wire with a clear narrative such as limited-partnership capital contribution, partner loan, or capital-account advance, and do not combine capital with customer receipts or unrelated third-party funds. Canada generally does not prescribe universal FX purpose codes; the remitting and receiving banks may require a payment purpose, source-of-funds declaration, beneficial-owner information, and supporting documents. Provide the partnership agreement, contribution or loan agreement, partner resolution, source-of-funds evidence, originator and beneficiary details, and expected-use schedule. Reconcile the bank receipt to the partnership ledger and preserve wire confirmations. Foreign-currency receipts may be retained or converted at the partnership's treasury discretion, subject to bank terms, accounting policy, tax treatment, and anti-money-laundering review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use Canadian domestic electronic funds transfer, wire transfer, or SWIFT MT103 for supplier and service-provider payments. Include complete originator, beneficiary, account, invoice, goods description, and payment-purpose information. For larger or higher-risk international purchases, use a documentary commercial letter of credit, standby letter of credit, documentary collection, or bank-guaranteed arrangement, subject to credit approval and applicable International Chamber of Commerce rules such as UCP 600 or URC 522. Match payments to purchase orders, commercial invoices, customs records, bills of lading or courier evidence, and supplier due diligence. For card and online sales, use Shopify Payments or Stripe only after confirming Canadian eligibility, settlement terms, reserve mechanics, chargeback allocation, prohibited-goods rules, and foreign-currency conversion pricing. Monitor sanctions, export controls, customs valuation, GST/QST treatment, and import-broker records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Canadian-dollar/foreign-currency forwards with an appropriately regulated Canadian bank or qualified dealer, supported by documented underlying exposures and counterparty limits

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency, jurisdiction, counterparty, and regulatory framework permit them; NDFs may be unsuitable for ordinary CAD exposure and require careful settlement, valuation, collateral, and legal-enforceability review

Currency swaps for structured or recurring funding exposures, subject to bank credit approval, ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms, accounting treatment, and applicable derivatives requirements

Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange options or collars for material forecast purchases or receipts, subject to suitability review, premium approval, counterparty documentation, and a prohibition on speculative trading

Internal hedging policy requiring documented exposure identification, hedge ratios, maturity limits, authorized counterparties, independent valuation, confirmation controls, accounting treatment, and quarterly effectiveness review

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual registration update (mise à jour annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the date on which the limited partnership was first registered in the Quebec enterprise register; the REQ sends an annual reminder.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to an administrative late fee; if the declaration remains unfiled, the REQ may, after prior notice, strike the LP from the register. The resulting absence of registration makes the partnership and its limited liability arrangements unavailable to be set up against third parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal partnership information return (T5013) and T5013 slips for each partner, if the partnership meets CRA filing thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period end (a December 31 year-end return is due in the following May/June calendar depending on the CRA filing rule applicable to partnerships).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalties for T5013 returns, late-slip penalties for each partner, and potential gross-negligence penalties for knowingly incomplete information.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit is imposed on a non-publicly accountable Quebec limited partnership. The obligation can arise contractually (partnership agreement, lender, or investor covenant) or by operation of a separate regulator if the LP carries on a regulated activity. The CBCA shareholder audit thresholds do not apply to a partnership.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook; a private limited partnership normally applies Part II (ASPE - Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) and may elect Part I (IFRS) if required or desired. IFRS is mandatory only for a publicly accountable partnership, which is uncommon for this factory/retail scope.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual REQ declaration is the statutory confirmation of the LP's partners and general partner; it must reflect the current partner composition. A transfer of a partnership interest is not reported on a separate UBO return; it is recorded by filing an updated declaration with REQ within the prescribed delay (normally 30 days after the change). Quebec's ultimate beneficiary register provisions apply to legal persons, not to the LP itself.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Partners) and Capital Contributions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No mandatory audit; voluntary/covenant-driven small private partnership audit typically USD 4,000 - USD 15,000 (CAD 5,500 - CAD 20,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: NIL at the Limited Partnership level (fiscally transparent flow-through). Applicable combined federal and Quebec general corporate rate for a corporate partner is 26.5% (15% federal + 11.5% Quebec); individual partners are taxed at progressive personal rates, plus the Quebec Health Contribution Fund where applicable.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays are not available in Canada. Preferential federal and Quebec deductions and credits include: Manufacturing and Processing Profits deduction (federal rate effectively reduced to 13% for qualifying manufacturing income); Small Business Deduction and Quebec SME deduction for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation partners; SR&ED investment tax credit at 15% of eligible expenditures (refundable portion available); and Quebec refundable credits for manufacturing and innovation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T5013 Information Return for Partnerships and Quebec TP-5013 Declaration de renseignements d'une societe de personnes; e-filing is mandatory through CRA NETFILE/E-file and Revenu Quebec's Transmissions electroniques / CLIC portal for partnerships with annual revenues above the prescribed threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (per partnership fiscal period, normally not exceeding 12 months)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than five months after the partnership fiscal-period end. For a December 31 year-end, the deadline is June 30 of the following calendar year; partners must receive their respective allocation slips before their own annual return filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, mailing address, jurisdiction of formation, Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), CRA business number and partnership registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not use a foreign address as the registered mailing address for the LP; provide non-resident partner identifying information only in the partner allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income and net business income (loss) of the partnership, computed on a fiscal-period basis, including all revenue from direct-to-consumer e-commerce sales and other receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate Canadian-source business income to each non-resident limited partner separately; identify income attributable to a permanent establishment in Quebec to ensure correct Part I taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner allocation schedule: full legal name, tax identification number, percentage ownership, share of income/loss, and amounts of guaranteed payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter foreign tax identification numbers for non-residents; mark treaty-protected amounts separately where a valid Form NR301 has been submitted, and attach a copy of each partner's tax residency certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: materials, subcontract labour, Shopify/Stripe processing fees, packaging, shipping, insurance, rent, depreciation, and other arm's-length costs; disallowed expenses must be added back.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners may not deduct Quebec-only expenses that are not economically linked to the Quebec permanent establishment; any such disallowance must be allocated back to the partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits of the partnership: SR&ED investment tax credits, Quebec refundable tax credits, and manufacturing-related credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: These credits generally flow through to Canadian resident partners; non-resident limited partners are not entitled to non-refundable provincial credits unless they file a Quebec return and satisfy the Quebec source-income conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or omission of the T5013/TP-5013 triggers CRA and Revenu Quebec daily surcharges of CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500 for most partnerships); larger partnerships exposed to enhanced daily penalties up to CAD 100 per day and maximum CAD 10,000; additional 10%-of-income administrative penalties and gross-negligence penalties may apply on reassessment, with normal limitation periods extended where misrepresentation or fraud is established.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: N/A — a Limited Partnership does not declare dividends. For distributions or allocations paid or credited to a non-resident limited partner, the statutory Part XIII withholding rate is 25% on the gross amount unless reduced by a tax treaty; active business income sourced to a Quebec permanent establishment may instead be taxed under Part I on a net basis.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident partner or its agent must provide to the partnership (payor/withholding agent) a fully completed Form NR301 (or applicable NR302/NR303) and the official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the partner's country of residence before the allocation is made. The GP must validate entitlement under the relevant Canada treaty, apply the reduced withholding rate at source, and retain the documentation in the partnership's books. If treaty relief was not claimed at source, the non-resident partner may file a Canadian tax return and use Form NR7 to request a refund of excess Part XIII withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Part XIII statutory rates: royalties paid or credited to a non-resident generally 25%; interest generally exempt from Part XIII withholding if arm's length and non-participating, otherwise subject to 25% if the non-resident holds significant equity or does not deal at arm's length. Treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 0% and royalties to 0-15%; for example, under the Canada-US DTA, interest is generally 0% and royalties generally 10% (0% for certain computer software/copyright payments), and under many European DTAs rates of 5% or 10% apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 Information Return for Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents must be filed where the aggregate fair market value of reportable cross-border transactions exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the fiscal period. Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File) should be prepared whenever such threshold is met; CBCR/Country-by-Country Reporting documentation is required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750,000,000 or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada and Quebec do not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the federal General Anti-Avoidance Rule (section 245, Income Tax Act), Quebec's equivalent GAAR (section 1079.1, Taxation Act), and CRA administrative practice require that a Quebec LP creates, manages, and executes genuine commercial activities in Quebec. For a custom mechanical keyboard keycap operation, economic substance is demonstrated by physical injection-moulding equipment, real inventory in Quebec, employees or subcontractors, management decisions, and commercial risk exposure. An LP with no office, no employees, and no local decision-making risks re-characterization as a sham or conduit without tax effect.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting e-commerce revenue from Shopify Payments or Stripe, fabricating supplier invoices, allocating profits to a tax-indifferent non-resident partner to avoid Canadian tax, or knowingly understating gross income on the T5013/TP-5013.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act section 239 and Quebec Taxation Act corresponding offences: fines from 50% to 200% of the tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment, and seizure of assets; CRA may also impose gross-negligence penalties of 50% of the understated tax and vacate the normal reassessment limitation period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable under section 227.1 of the Income Tax Act for unremitted withholding taxes and interest if not exercised reasonable care; criminal conviction for evasion allows civil recovery against personal assets, court-ordered travel restrictions, bail conditions, and extradition exposure in cases involving cross-border concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering the Quebec LP solely as a billing conduit for foreign-owned keycap sales, with no premises, no equipment, no employees, no stock, and total dependence on offshore management; interposing the LP to avoid Quebec QST and GST/HST obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR permits CRA and Revenu Quebec to deny the tax benefit, reallocate income to the actual economic operator, and assess gross-negligence penalties plus interest; Revenu Quebec can cancel QST registrations retroactively and deem a permanent establishment in Quebec on the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil will be pierced where the LP is a mere instrumentality; general partners and directing minds are personally liable for unremitted GST/QST and unpaid corporate taxes, and risk personal disqualification orders and asset freezes in civil enforcement proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling custom keycaps to a related offshore wholesale entity at below-cost or non-arm's-length margins, shifting profit via inflated management fees, failure to file Form T106, or not retaining contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation after the CAD 1,000,000 threshold is crossed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under section 247 of the Income Tax Act, CRA may adjust the transaction to arm's-length terms and impose a penalty equal to 10% of the net adjustment where the taxpayer fails to make reasonable efforts; interest accrues from the original due date, and the T106 filing omission itself attracts daily information-return penalties up to CAD 2,500; double taxation may be mitigated only through mutual agreement procedure under the applicable DTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved non-arm's-length arrangements can be named in a penalty assessment under section 247 as 'liable persons'; in fraud cases, personal liability for the company's tax debt may be asserted through the unpaid-source-deduction provisions and civil conspiracy claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the opaque LP structure to receive e-commerce proceeds through third-party MSBs without identification, structuring transactions below reporting thresholds, or accepting unexplained cash payments without complying with record-keeping and verification obligations despite the low-risk standard tier applied to the activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 for a first violation; knowing money laundering is a criminal offence punishable by up to 5 years imprisonment; Revenu Quebec and FINTRAC may freeze accounts and confiscate property connected to the unlawful activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and directors who knowingly controlled or facilitated the structuring are criminally liable despite the LP's limited liability; the limited liability shield is forfeited for personal participation in an offence, and individuals face arrest warrants, bail travel restrictions, and orders of restitution or forfeiture.
